answer: A summit looks the same from every trail, so the coop checks the ground: an inspector walks the parcel, counts bearing walnut trees against the county assessor map, and files one lot number per parcel. The node reads that filing and rechecks it after each harvest, so two seats on one parcel cancel. Fifty clones need fifty bearing orchards. Land runs 40,000 dollars an acre, three years to first crop, irrigation 6,500, so a cohort ties up near 2.3 million before a hull dries. The coop ledger mirrors the assessor map, so a copied lot number points at ground the copier does not own.
